What the summer of 2022 taught Jackson businesses

The city went under a boil water notice on July 29, 2022. Late in August, flooding on the Pearl River pushed the O.B. Curtis treatment plant, already running on backup pumps, to the point of failure. State officials announced on August 29 that the system was failing, and the governor declared a state of emergency the next day. About 600 members of the Mississippi National Guard were sent to help hand out water.

Restaurants felt it at once. The state hospitality and restaurant association said many of the roughly 500 restaurants in the area were having problems with the water. Owners drove to neighboring towns for ice, bought canned drinks and disposable plates, and reported thousands of dollars a week in extra costs. At least one Fondren restaurant cited the water troubles when it closed for good that fall. In November 2022, a federal judge put an interim third-party manager in charge of the water system, which now runs as JXN Water.

Through all of it, customers had one question for every business: are you open, and is it safe? The owners who could answer it on their own website, quickly and clearly, spent less of the day on the phone.

How an update-ready site handles a bad morning

  1. A banner that is already builtWe can leave room at the top of your home page for a short notice, kept empty until you need it.
  2. One message to MauriceEmail or call with the wording, or just the facts, and he writes it up and posts it. Updates are part of maintenance.
  3. The same words everywhereThe notice goes on the home page and the hours or contact page, and you change your Google Business Profile so search shows the same story.
  4. Back to normalWhen things settle, the banner comes down and your regular hours go back up. Nothing else on the site has to change.

Website design Jackson MS neighborhoods each need differently

Jackson is the state capital, and its customers sort themselves by neighborhood. A site that says only "Jackson" misses how people actually search and talk.

Fondren

North State Street is the main drag, lined with boutiques, galleries and neighborhood restaurants. On Fondren's First Thursday, a free evening that runs most months from spring into fall, shops and restaurants stay open late and spill onto the sidewalks while bands play. A Fondren shop's site should list that night's hours and specials.

Belhaven

A neighborhood inside the city, close to Fondren and downtown, known for its green spaces and a wide mix of architecture. Home service trades, tutors, therapists and small studios who work there do well with a page that names it.

Farish Street

Carved out in the 1870s and 1880s, Farish Street became the center of Black business life in Jackson under segregation, with lawyers, doctors, funeral homes, clubs and record labels such as Trumpet Records. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980. Revival plans have stalled more than once, and anyone opening there is building on a long story worth telling on the about page.

Jackson State University

A public HBCU founded in 1877 as Natchez Seminary in Natchez, later moved to Jackson, on John R. Lynch Street. Student housing, food, printing, barbers and tutoring around campus all rise and fall with the academic calendar, and their sites should say so.

Across the county lines, Ridgeland and Madison sit north in Madison County, and Brandon and Flowood sit east in Rankin County. Each is its own town with its own searches. Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence, so a Flowood customer is more likely to see a business whose site actually talks about Flowood. A real page for each town you serve does that honestly. Nobody can promise a ranking, and we do not.

Common questions

How much does web design in Jackson, MS cost?

Prices around Jackson run from a builder's monthly fee you do yourself to agency quotes that only come after a meeting. Ours are printed and paid once: Starter is $497 for five hand-written pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten researched city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for keyword research and a page for every town and service pairing worth targeting. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Is there web design for Mississippi businesses outside Jackson?

Yes. We work remotely, so a shop in Hattiesburg, Tupelo or the Delta gets the same process as one on North State Street: a free demo first, pages written by hand for your business and your towns, and the same printed prices. We are in East Texas, not Mississippi, and we say so plainly.

If my business has to close suddenly, how do I tell customers on my website?

Send Maurice the notice by email or call (903) 636-7511, and it goes in a banner at the top of your home page, with the same wording on your hours or contact page. Updates are covered by your maintenance plan, so the notice itself costs nothing extra. Change your Google Business Profile hours at the same time so search results and your site say the same thing.

Can you make website design for Jackson MS and the suburbs work on one site?

Yes, with a separate page for each place you really serve. Someone in Ridgeland, Madison, Brandon or Flowood searches by their own town. Pro includes ten city pages, each researched and written for that town, and Agency begins with keyword research across the metro to decide which towns are worth a page.

Do you have an office in Jackson?

No. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson in Big Sandy, East Texas, and every site is built remotely. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour: an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.
